headline: High-risk shared-workspace pair: CrewAI can write broad host files while Semantica reads/writes many data sources and MCP resources, creating dangerous leakage, conflict, and cascade paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can read/write the host working directory and uses shared memory by default; Semantica can ingest local files, web pages, email, Git, and MCP resources. That creates a plausible instruction-hijack path if one agent’s outputs are placed where the other parses them as trusted content. The pairwise bridge is documented in both profiles, but not as a direct exploit.
conditions: IF CrewAI outputs are written into a directory Semantica ingests automatically, injection risk is present.
IF Semantica parses CrewAI-generated files as instructions or provenance, prompt hijack becomes plausible.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories.
Disable automatic ingestion of CrewAI output files.
Add a human review step before Semantica consumes CrewAI artifacts.
Use provenance tags or allowlists for files passed between agents.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation at the handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI touches developer-passed crew data and handles API keys; Semantica touches enterprise data, contracts, decision records, secrets, and many file/API surfaces. Because CrewAI has broad filesystem and browser access and Semantica can read local files, databases, email, and MCP resources, the default pair can expose sensitive data across the boundary unless tightly isolated.
conditions: IF both agents share a workspace or mounted volume, sensitive files can flow from one to the other.
IF CrewAI receives secrets or customer data and Semantica ingests local files or MCP resources, leakage risk is active.
mitigations: Run the agents in separate containers or workspaces.
Remove secrets from any shared directory before handoff.
Restrict Semantica to a read-only, minimal input set.
Disable browser/file access for CrewAI when handling sensitive data.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention and access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; Semantica can also write the filesystem, modify git state, install packages, and use MCP. Both support multiple instances, but CrewAI has developer-defined shared state while Semantica uses a single shared intelligence layer, so concurrent writes to shared resources can collide and corrupt state or repositories.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or git repository, write conflicts are possible.
IF Semantica modifies git state while CrewAI writes files concurrently, state corruption can occur.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate writable directory.
Serialize writes with a lock file or orchestrator mutex.
Prevent CrewAI from writing into Semantica-managed repositories.
Pause one agent before the other mutates shared state.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI’s role-playing crews can emit outputs that Semantica may ingest from files, APIs, or MCP resources. Semantica’s deterministic graph/provenance tooling can still propagate bad upstream facts if they are treated as authoritative inputs. Because both agents can act on shared artifacts, an error in CrewAI can cascade into downstream decisions or records in Semantica.
conditions: IF Semantica consumes CrewAI output without verification, upstream mistakes can propagate.
IF CrewAI-generated facts are written into Semantica-managed records, downstream decisions may be wrong.
mitigations: Require explicit verification before Semantica accepts CrewAI outputs.
Keep CrewAI outputs as drafts, not source-of-truth records.
Add checksum or provenance checks at the handoff.
Limit Semantica to read-only evaluation of CrewAI artifacts.
requires-engineering: implement validation gates between generation and ingestion.

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, while Semantica touches enterprise data, contracts, audit trails, and secrets. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so a compliance breach is not proven; however, the pair clearly mixes sensitive data classes with broad network/file/MCP surfaces, making policy mismatch plausible and requiring explicit controls.
conditions: IF regulated data such as contracts, audit trails, or secrets flows through both agents, retention and access policies must align.
IF either agent is deployed in a jurisdiction or certification regime not covered by the other, compliance mismatch becomes material.
mitigations: Document the data classes allowed through each agent.
Align retention and deletion settings before deployment.
Block regulated data from any non-approved path.
Review vendor residency and certification claims.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
